Left: the middle edge B-C alone; both other edges touch B or C, so nothing can be added and is_maximal_matching() returns True. Right: A-B alone; the edge C-D (shown in the accent color with its free endpoints C and D) could still be added, so is_maximal_matching() returns False." width="100%"} A matching is a set of edges with no shared endpoints. It is *maximal* when no other edge of the graph can be added without breaking that rule: every edge has at least one endpoint that is already matched. Maximal is weaker than maximum (largest possible): `maximal_matching()` returns maximal matchings quickly, while `maximum_weight_matching()` on an unweighted graph returns a maximum one, and every maximum matching is maximal. Edge direction is ignored. Self-loops cannot be part of a matching, and they are not needed to make it maximal. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [edges]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [list[int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A list of integer edge IDs, such as the output of `maximal_matching()`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : `True` if the edges exist, form a matching, and no edge can be added to it. Unknown edge IDs give `False`. ::: ## Technical Notes {.doc-technical-notes} The check marks the matched nodes and then makes one pass over the edges, looking for a non-loop edge whose two endpoints are both unmatched. It runs in $O(V + E)$. ## Examples {.doc-examples} In the path A-B-C-D, the middle edge alone is maximal (both outer edges touch B or C), but not maximum, and the single outer edge A-B is not even maximal: ::: {#36a02898 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec g = ec.Graph().add_nodes(["A", "B", "C", "D"]) g.add_edges([("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) ab, bc, cd = (g.find_edge_ids(u, v)[0] for u, v in [("A", "B"), ("B", "C"), ("C", "D")]) g.is_maximal_matching([bc]), g.is_maximal_matching([ab]), g.is_maximal_matching([ab, cd]) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (True, False, True) ``` ::: :::
